news.headline: Softbank further trims India exposure, sells Meesho shares worth ₹1,885 cr
news.summary: Japanese investor SoftBank Group has sold 1.65 per cent stake in Meesho for Rs 1,885 crore, further trimming its investments in India's e-commerce sector. In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore. With this, the affiliate's holding in Meesho has fallen to 5.19 per cent from 6.84 per cent. The stake sale, however, found buyers, with a clutch of domestic and foreign institutional investors participating in the transaction, with Societe Generale (SocGen) emerging as the largest buyer. Paris-based financial services firm SocGen picked up more than 1.47 crore shares, or a 0.32 per cent stake, for Rs 364.65 crore. Domestic institutional buyers included mutual funds managed by Motilal Oswal, HDFC, ...
news.takeaway: Japanese investor SoftBank Group has sold 1.65 per cent stake in Meesho for Rs 1,885 crore, further trimming; institutional flow is the domestic risk check; price still has to confirm it after the first hour.
news.whyItMatters: FII/DII direction can explain whether global cues are being absorbed or rejected by local cash-market demand.
news.indiaImpact: Nifty and Bank Nifty need market participation aligned with FII/DII flow before the morning bias deserves follow-through weight.
